numeric_arrays.binary64: float[] - runtime-sized array of `float` (IEEE-754 binary64), created with array(n, fill = 0.0) and indexed with [i]
numeric_arrays.integer64: int[] - runtime-sized array of `int` (signed 64-bit), created with array(n, fill = 0)
numeric_arrays.allocation: value semantics; arrays are contiguous native storage with bounds and initialization checks; workload arrays are passed to helpers by reference (`int[] &`) so no copy is made except where the workload itself copies (MB-07's per-round copy is an ordinary value assignment)

string_buffer.buffer: uint8[] - the mutable byte buffer used by MB-08 passes 1-4; obtained once before the timed region from the joined text with uint8[](text.utf8())
string_buffer.string: string - immutable UTF-8 text; built fresh inside each MB-08 round from the buffer with string.from_utf8(bin(buffer))
string_buffer.string_access: string.codepoints() - the string type's own scalar-sequence accessor, iterated in order for MB-08 pass 5
string_buffer.direct_character_access: yes: text[index] returns a one-code-point string and .codepoints() returns the scalar sequence

file_io.writer: file.create(path) -> file.Handle, then Handle.write(text) per line, Handle.flush(), Handle.close()
file_io.reader: file.open(path) -> file.Handle, then Handle.read_line() -> string | none | error until none
file_io.incremental: true - the handle API writes and reads incrementally; the runtime's handle buffering is not user-configurable, so the frozen 65536-byte buffer size cannot be requested and the language's own buffering is what is measured (recorded here as required by micro.md section 4.12(c))

collections.map: map.Map<int, int> - the standard insertion-ordered open-addressing map; default construction, get(k) -> int | none, set, has, remove, keys(), values()
collections.set: set.Set<int> - the standard insertion-ordered set; default construction
collections.allocator: the language's ordinary managed value storage; no allocator choice exists

monotonic_clock.api: time.now() -> time.Instant and time.since(start) -> time.Duration; elapsed nanoseconds are math.round(duration.seconds() * 1000000000.0)

runtime_checks.effective_behavior: always on under the frozen recipe `quidra build FILE.qui -o BIN`: integer overflow, division by zero, array bounds, uninitialized reads, numeric cast range and the call-depth guard terminate deterministically with status 101; native code is otherwise optimized with Clang -O3 without fast-math
